papers_read.title_as_printed: Deep learning combining FDG-PET and neurocognitive data accurately predicts MCI conversion to Alzheimer's dementia 3-year post MCI diagnosis (Cao, Ma, Nayak, Duong, Neurobiology of Disease 187 (2023) 106310)
Dual attention based fusion network for MCI Conversion Prediction (Luo, He, Cui, Ward, Chen, Computers in Biology and Medicine 182 (2024) 109039)

what_each_reports.P-81: 3D CNN on whole-brain baseline FDG-PET, transfer-learned from an AD vs CN model, combined with age and five cognitive scores (CDR-SB, logical memory delayed recall, MMSE, mPACC digit and trails B), ADNI1/2/GO, 257 MCI (164 stable/93 converting within 3 years). Best model PET+Age+CS: balanced accuracy 0.7326 +/- 0.0978, AUC 0.7849 +/- 0.0963 (5-fold cross-validation, mean +/- SD). PET alone: BA 0.565, AUC 0.610.
what_each_reports.P-8: Dual attention fusion network: 3D ShuffleNet V2 on baseline T1 MRI with neurocognitive metadata (age, sex, APOE4, MMSE, CDR-SB, ADAS-cog, seven FreeSurfer volumes) guiding spatial attention and fused by self-attention, ADNI1/2, 298 sMCI/295 pMCI (36-month conversion), Wen et al. splits, 5-fold CV: accuracy 81.34% (variance 0.001), AUC 0.874, sensitivity 0.85, specificity 0.78 (so balanced accuracy about 0.815). Metadata alone (SVM) reaches 78.75%, AUC 0.868.

quantity_a: Balanced accuracy for 3-year MCI-to-AD conversion from baseline FDG-PET + age + five cognitive scores, ADNI, 257 MCI (36% converters)
quantity_b: Accuracy for 36-month MCI-to-AD conversion from baseline structural MRI + demographic, APOE4, cognitive and volumetric metadata, ADNI, 593 MCI (50% converters)
incompatible_if_same: No. P-8's balanced accuracy of about 0.815 lies within one fold-SD of P-81's 0.733 +/- 0.098, and P-81's AUC 0.785 +/- 0.096 likewise brackets P-8's 0.874 within one SD. Neither paper claims an ordering against the other's method (P-8 compares itself with MRI-only methods such as CAAT, not with P-81).

gates.task: match: both 3-year (36-month) MCI conversion to AD (T2)
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (different, partly overlapping MCI subsets)
gates.validation_tier: match: both internal 5-fold cross-validation, no external cohort
gates.modality_family: mismatch: FDG-PET (metabolic) plus cognitive scores vs structural MRI plus cognitive, genetic and volumetric metadata. The earlier rejection recorded this mismatch; the record's modality_family 'LanguageBehavior' is wrong for both

endpoint_and_metric: partly compatible: same endpoint and horizon, but balanced accuracy (P-81) vs accuracy (P-8, near-balanced classes, so accuracy is close to balanced accuracy) and different predictor sets (different imaging modality and different cognitive/genetic covariates, e.g. ADAS-cog and APOE4 only in P-8)
performance_validity: flag does not apply: neither reaches 0.97 on the conversion task (P-81's 1.000 values are for AD vs CN with cognitive scores, which the authors attribute to scores that define AD, not the conversion task).
independence: Both use ADNI, so MCI subjects overlap in part. Different groups (Albert Einstein/Wake Forest/Weill Cornell; La Trobe), no shared authors.
grounds: The two results are compatible: P-8's balanced accuracy (about 0.815) and AUC (0.874) fall within one fold-SD of P-81's 0.733 +/- 0.098 and 0.785 +/- 0.096.
Neither paper claims an ordering relative to the other's method, so the difference is two methods reporting different scores, which the rule does not read as incompatible.

The quantities also differ (FDG-PET vs structural MRI as the imaging input, different cognitive and genetic covariates, 36% vs 50% converters), and the modality-family gate fails with no waiver; either ground alone would close the pair.

evidence_quotes.quote: the best model was a combination of FDG-PET, age, and neurocognitive data, yielding an AUC of 0.785 +/- 0.096 and a balanced accuracy of 0.733 +/- 0.098.

The final cohort that met the criteria contained a total of 612 subjects, including 205 patients with the diagnosis of Dementia of Alzheimer's type (DAT), 150 cognitively normal subjects, 164 stable-MCI subjects, and 93 unstable-MCI subjects.
Balanced accuracy (BA), specificity, sensitivity, and AUC of the validation sets were obtained using 5-fold cross validation. Values shown are mean +/- standard deviation.
The experimental results show that our proposed model achieves an accuracy, AUC, and sensitivity of 81.34%, 0.874, and 0.85 respectively using 5-fold cross validation evaluation.
The dataset comprises of 593 MRI images of 298 sMCIs and 295 pMCIs retrieved from datasets ADNI1 and ADNI2.

record_defects: modality_family 'LanguageBehavior' is wrong: P-81 is FDG-PET plus cognitive scores, P-8 is structural MRI plus neurocognitive metadata.
modality_family_equal='Yes' contradicts the record's own resolution note ('Modality mismatch: P-81=PET vs P-8=structural_MRI'), which the PDFs support.
claim_a compares P-81's balanced accuracy with P-8's plain accuracy without noting the metric difference (small here because P-8's classes are near-balanced).
The bridging list (C-index, nomogram and other-task papers) is not apt for this pair.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in the two documents; a disagreement would need estimates on a shared imaging modality and predictor set whose uncertainty excludes each other, which neither paper provides.
